Velocity-driven Disney motion smear and squash-stretch

I wanted to know if one ElementGL canvas can stretch, squash and smear a live HTML card from its instantaneous velocity, then snap back to crisp 1:1 text and hit-testing when it stops. Drag and fling the card, press Fling card, or toggle Figure-8 orbit.

Show the code Live drawable card, 2D spring-damper physics, squash-stretch smear shader and hit sync
  1. Live card inside one drawable canvas. #ms-card sits inside <canvas id="ms-canvas" content="drawable" layoutsubtree> with an editable label, palette buttons and +1 Ping counter.
  2. 2D momentum, spring-damper physics and hit-box sync. stepCardMotion(state, tMs) bounces softly off stage bounds, couples the figure-8 orbit via a damped spring, and calls updateElementGeometry() with geometryUnit() and data-hit-tick.
  3. Squash-stretch, 16-tap smear and chromatic RGB trail shader. SMEAR_FRAG warps coordinates along uVel with stretch * squash == 1.0, integrates 16 dithered taps with leading warm and trailing cool fringes, and snaps to 1:1 when speed < 0.01.
  4. Premultiplied uploads, 5-arg 2D fallback and context recovery. Turns on UNPACK_PREMULTIPLY_ALPHA_WEBGL, gates stage.upload() on paint after stage.begin(), and moves the card into #plain-host on webglcontextlost.

How it works

One <canvas id="ms-canvas" content="drawable" layoutsubtree> holds #ms-card under a single ElementGL WebGL 2 context from /lib/element-gl.js. Both creation and onRestored turn on gl.pixelStorei(gl.UNPACK_PREMULTIPLY_ALPHA_WEBGL, true) so the rounded borders, colour swatches and text keep clean edges over the dark stage grid. Texture uploads wait for hasPainted = true inside paint after calling stage.begin(), so the backing store matches device pixel ratio before stage.upload() copies the card.

Dragging, flinging, Fling card or Figure-8 orbit drives stepCardMotion(state, tMs) with explicit timestamps. Free flings coast under exponential damping with soft elastic wall rebounds inside the stage margins; Reset centre and Figure-8 orbit pull the card with a 2D spring-damper. Each frame passes the normalised velocity vector uVel to SMEAR_FRAG on a padded local quad so trails never clip at the card border.

Inside SMEAR_FRAG, any frame with speed >= 0.01 computes an area-preserving basis aligned to (vx, vy) (stretch = 1 + 0.24 * min(speed, 2.2), squash = 1 / stretch) and integrates 16 interleaved-gradient-noise taps weighted from the leading edge into the trailing wake, splitting red ahead and blue behind for a chromatic RGB trail. Once speed < 0.01 or Compare crisp 1:1 (no smear) is pressed, the shader takes one direct unpadded texture sample with zero blur. Every position or stretch change updates updateElementGeometry() scaled by geometryUnit() and flips data-hit-tick to clear Chromium's hit-test cache, while IntersectionObserver and document.hidden pause the loop off screen. If WebGL 2 is unavailable or ?route=2d is set, a 5-argument drawElementImage() trail renders instead; on webglcontextlost or ?route=plain, the live card moves into #plain-host as plain HTML.

Live checks

These checks run on isolated fixtures inside testStage() and wait for a tap so opening the page doesn't allocate extra WebGL contexts or move focus.

StatusCheckDetail

Findings

  • Measured in HeadlessChrome/160.0.0.0 on 2026-11-27 (412 px wide, DPR 2.625, with CanvasDrawElement enabled): all 6 live checks pass with 0 console errors, scrollWidth === 412, a 945×961 backing store (0.91 MP, 7.27 MB initial, 16.78 MB peak), glPeak = 2, glActive = 1 after checks, removed = 0, openSnapshots = 0, unaskedReads = 0, noSizeDraws = 0 and wrongDraws = 0.
  • Under diagonal velocity (+1.2, -0.9), area-preserving deformation measured stretch = 1.45x and squash = 0.69x (product 1.00), while trailing wake luminance jumped from 13 at rest (and 13 perpendicular) to 124 on mobile (141 at 960 px desktop), with separated trailing blue rgb(86, 125, 162) and leading red rgb(78, 7, 14) chromatic fringes. Turning on Compare crisp 1:1 (no smear) returned trailing edge luminance to 13 immediately while the card kept moving along the figure-8 path.
  • Deterministic stepCardMotion(state, tMs) coasted across 5 wall bounces (peak speed 2.37) to vel = 0 inside stage bounds, sprang cleanly back to centre (66, 91), and snapped in one step under reduced motion. Real CDP clicks and text input hit +1 Ping (1 ping), switched palette to cobalt, appended text inside #ms-title-input, and clicked +1 Ping again at its displaced post-fling settle (70, 145) (2 pings).
  • With ?route=2d, the 5-argument drawElementImage() trail ran at 1621 px/s (1.53x/0.65x) with noSizeDraws = 0 and wrongDraws = 0. With ?route=plain or --disable-blink-features=CanvasDrawElement, #ms-card moved into #plain-host (scrollWidth = 412). Under emulated prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, Figure-8 orbit stayed off and Fling card stepped with 0 px/s and zero smear.
  • Running /lib/a11y-audit.js at 960×800 with focus emulation passed 9 checks (calm, blank, dom, hit, ghost, focus 6/6, names 6/6, sharp, motion) with 0 failures and 1 warning (zoom, because ElementGL.#syncSize() doesn't scale backing pixels by currentCSSZoom).
  • npm run check:jank, node tools/draw-size/audit.mjs, real Chrome 159 on Android hardware and social.jpg capture are not verified yet.
